name: Pre-College Scholars Program (University of Maryland)
org: University of Maryland, A. James Clark School of Engineering
what_you_do: Spend three weeks on the UMD campus. You get about 38 hours of SAT prep and 11 hours of college prep. You also hear department talks and join admissions and financial aid workshops. You get one on one help with college applications.
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (currently in 10th or 11th grade)
who_can_apply: Students who go to high school in Maryland or Washington, D.C., or live there. You need a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5. You must show interest and skill in math, science or engineering.
pay_detail: The whole program costs $400 per student. Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.
duration: Three weeks, in person on the UMD campus. The 2026 session ran Monday July 6 to Friday July 24.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was Friday May 8, 2026, with notices by May 22 and rolling spots after that. The 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Online application with a one page personal statement (12 point, double spaced), an official high school transcript, and official PSAT or SAT scores if you have them. You must attend all sessions, orientation, and the pre and post tests. Contact: Ms. Aishah Briscoe, FutureEngineer@umd.edu.
notes: The page does not say whether the program is residential. Costs money but is low compared with most pre-college programs. Dates and the $400 price are from the 2026 page.
